questions.text: Which three financial criteria are used to evaluate IT project selection, per the material?
questions.explanation: Projects are evaluated via Payback Period, Return on Investment (ROI), and Net Present Value (NPV).

questions.text: What does "Payback Period" measure?
options: The time required to recover the initial IT investment
The total lifetime profit of a project
The discount rate applied to cash flows
questions.explanation: Payback Period is the time required to recover the initial IT investment.

questions.text: What does ROI (Return on Investment) measure?
options: Net profit generated relative to cost
questions.explanation: ROI is net profit generated relative to cost.

questions.text: What does NPV (Net Present Value) calculate?
options: Total expected monetary gain by discounting future cash flows to present-day value
questions.explanation: NPV calculates total expected monetary gain by discounting future cash flows to present-day value.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as strategic / non-financial drivers for project selection?
questions.explanation: The listed non-financial drivers are Regulatory Compliance, System Reliability, Competitive Necessity, and Social Responsibility. Projects driven by these are often selected regardless of ROI.

questions.text: Match each strategic / non-financial driver to its description.
allChoices: Navigating mandatory legal requirements (e.g., anti-money laundering laws, Data Privacy)
Core infrastructure modernizations to prevent catastrophic downtime during peak operational hours
Implementing baseline technological capabilities required to match industry market standards
Projects strategically advancing SDG goals like decent work and economic growth

pairs.match: Navigating mandatory legal requirements (e.g., anti-money laundering laws, Data Privacy)
Core infrastructure modernizations to prevent catastrophic downtime during peak operational hours

questions.explanation: Each strategic driver maps to a distinct description from the course material.

questions.text: In the EduTech Solutions case scenario, what was Option A's (Cloud Migration) initial cost?
questions.explanation: Option A (Cloud Migration) had an initial cost of $150,000.

questions.text: In the EduTech Solutions case scenario, what was Option B's (Mobile QR Feature) estimated ROI?
questions.explanation: Option B (Mobile QR Feature) had an estimated ROI of 35%, versus 15% for Option A.

questions.text: In the EduTech Solutions case, Option B (Mobile QR Feature) had a longer payback period than Option A (Cloud Migration).
questions.explanation: Option B's payback period was 1.0 year, shorter than Option A's 2.5 years.

questions.text: Despite Option B offering superior ROI, why did executives choose Option A in the EduTech Solutions case?
options: Platform stability during exam weeks was a non-negotiable strategic necessity
The sponsor preferred Option A personally
Option B had no identified risks
questions.explanation: Executives selected Option A because platform stability during exam weeks (System Stability & SLA Compliance) was a non-negotiable strategic necessity.

questions.text: In the PMBOK Initiating Process Group workflow shown, what precedes the Business Case?
questions.explanation: The workflow flows: Business Need -> Business Case -> Selection Criteria -> Project Charter.

questions.text: What does the Business Case validate?
questions.explanation: The Business Case is a formal proposal validating cost versus strategic benefits.

questions.text: Which of the following are listed as Key Elements of a Project Charter?
questions.explanation: Key charter elements include Project Purpose, SMART Objectives, Scope Boundaries, Key Constraints, Summary Milestones, and PM Authority. A detailed WBS belongs in the project plan, not the charter.

questions.text: SMART Objectives establish specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and ___-bound success criteria.
questions.explanation: SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound.

questions.text: In the Digital KYC Engine case, what percentage customer drop-off does Zenith Bank experience due to its manual onboarding process?
questions.explanation: Zenith Bank experiences a 40% customer drop-off due to its 3-day manual account creation process.

questions.text: What is the target account creation processing time defined in the KYC project's success criteria?
questions.explanation: The success criteria requires account creation processing time reliably completed in under 10 minutes.

questions.text: What is the budget cap defined as a key constraint in the Digital KYC charter?
questions.explanation: The key constraint states a strict financial constraint: budget capped at $200,000.

questions.text: Under the PM Authority Level in the Digital KYC case, what percentage of total contingency funds can the PM reallocate without board review?
questions.explanation: The PM is authorized to reallocate up to 10% of total contingency funds and approve internal schedule adjustments under 5 days without board review.

questions.text: What pitfall occurs when a charter is written too high-level, lacking clear boundaries?
options: It directly invites Scope Creep by acting as a blank check
It becomes too expensive to print
It eliminates the need for an RTM
questions.explanation: A charter lacking boundaries acts as a blank check, directly inviting immediate Scope Creep.

questions.text: What pitfall occurs from writing a full WBS inside the charter itself?
options: It forces constant formal rework when initial assumptions change
It makes the charter too short
It removes the need for stakeholder sign-off
questions.explanation: Writing a WBS inside the charter forces constant formal rework when initial assumptions change.

questions.text: A Project Charter is the same thing as a project plan.
questions.explanation: The material states a charter is NOT a project plan -- the Charter authorizes WHAT and WHY, while the RTM and WBS dictate HOW.

questions.text: The phrase "Speed Dating for Ideas" is used as an analogy for which concept?
questions.explanation: Project Selection is described as "Speed Dating for Ideas" -- rigorously evaluating competing initiatives to pick the one with maximum business value.

questions.text: The phrase "The Birth Certificate & Contract" is used as an analogy for which concept?
questions.explanation: The Project Charter is described as "The Birth Certificate & Contract" -- it officially establishes the project's existence and empowers the PM.
